gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-liter: Liter sets plain sans letters with zero stroke contrast, upright lowercase and wide mouths on every round form. Beside Electroharmonix, it feels like a hush after a shout.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-matangi: Electroharmonix makes a striking entrance, breaking its lettering apart with open gaps and giving every round character an open-handed curve. Matangi, sans-serif with twine-like strokes, handles the hefty lowercase work.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-maven-pro: Visible gaps split the letters of Electroharmonix apart, a striking look that announces itself at once. And Maven Pro, sans-serif with a high-waisted lowercase, hums softly beneath it, so let the heading take the larger size.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-michroma: Michroma gives every letter a wide berth on both sides. Down a full page it would feel wide and spacious, curves leaving daylight, with Electroharmonix as the striking voice above.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-mozilla-he: Electroharmonix is striking, with open gaps between its letters. It does best at commanding attention, whereas Mozilla Headline, sans-serif with big-bodied letters and a splayed c terminal, does best at feeling approachable.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-mozilla-te: Striking from the first glance, Electroharmonix opens gaps between its letters and gives round characters open-handed curves. Mozilla Text, a sans with outward-flaring terminals and bold-looking lowercase, does the steadier work.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-nobile: Gaps that split the letters apart define Electroharmonix, a striking, open-handed face. Nobile, plain sans with lowercase nearly matching its capitals, would run down a page smoothly, letter mouths open like chalk arcs left unjoined.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-nokora: Gaps between the letters are the whole personality of Electroharmonix, striking and open-handed in every curve. Nokora, sans-serif with a wide-open s, lays a thick, dark stripe of lowercase across each line, friendly and solid.
